name: Basantapur (Kathmandu) Durbar Square
description:
Location:
Kathmandu Durbar Square (Basantapur) is located in the historic center of Kathmandu, bounded by Makhan to the northeast, New Road to the south, and Maru to the southwest.

Existence:
Enlisted as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979, the square has roots in the Licchavi era (3rd to 8th centuries CE), reaching architectural maturity under the Malla and Shah dynasties from the 16th through 19th centuries.

Description:
Durbar Square is an extraordinary open-air museum of traditional Newar architecture, comprising more than twenty palaces, pagoda temples, courtyards (chowks), and monumental stone sculptures.

Basantapur Tower (Nautale Durbar)

The Basantapur Tower is the tallest structure in the royal palace of Hanuman Dhoka. Standing nine storeys high, this tower was constructed between 1768 and 1775 by King Prithvi Narayan Shah and King Pratap Singh Shah to commemorate the unification of the Kathmandu Valley.

Gaddi Baithak

Built in 1908 by Rana Prime Minister Chandra Shumsher in European neoclassical style, Gaddi Baithak was historically used for state banquets, royal receptions, and welcoming foreign ambassadors. Today it houses museum exhibitions documenting modern Nepalese political history.

Kumari Chhen (Kumari Ghar)

The Kumari Ghar is a richly carved three-storey Newar residential palace built in 1757 by King Jaya Prakash Malla. It serves as the official sanctuary and residence of the Living Goddess (Kumari), the royal reincarnation of Goddess Taleju/Durga.

Trailokya Mohan Narayan Temple

An elegant five-plinth, three-tiered pagoda built in 1679 by Parthivendra Malla in memory of his brother Nripendra Malla. Dedicated to Vishnu of the Three Worlds, it is flanked by a famous kneeling stone statue of Garuda erected in 1689.

Kasthamandap (Maru Sata)

Kasthamandap (literally 'wooden covered pavilion') is an ancient three-tiered public assembly hall from which Kathmandu derives its name. Tracing to the 12th century or earlier, tradition holds that it was constructed from the timber of a single Sal tree.

Maju Dega Temple

Built in 1690 by Queen Mother Riddhi Laxmi during the reign of young King Bhupalendra Malla, this monumental three-tiered Shiva temple dominates the square from atop a massive nine-stage brick plinth.

Shiva Parvati Temple

Constructed in the late 18th century during the reign of King Rana Bahadur Shah, this rectangular two-storey temple features painted wooden figures of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati looking out from the upper central window.

Bhagawati Temple

A five-level temple with three Newar pagoda tiers, built by King Jagajjaya Malla (1722-1736). Originally enshrining Mahipatindreshwor Narayan, King Prithvi Narayan Shah installed an image of Goddess Bhagawati brought from Nuwakot.

Taleju Bell and Two Big Drums

Erected in 1797 by King Rana Bahadur Shah, the great bronze Taleju Bell is struck 108 times alongside two large ceremonial drums during daily worship at Taleju Bhawani.

Shwet Bhairav

A giant sculpted mask of Shwet Bhairav installed in 1795 under King Rana Bahadur Shah. Kept behind an ornate carved wooden latticed window, the fierce golden face is revealed to the public only during the annual Indra Jatra festival.

Dega Taleju Temple

Built in 1564 by King Mahendra Malla, this is the second tallest temple in Basantapur. Dedicated to Goddess Taleju Bhawani, its architectural floor plan is shaped as a cosmic Yantra.

Vamsha Gopal (Krishna) Temple

An octagonal two-tiered temple constructed in 1648 during the reign of King Pratap Malla, locally called Chyasilin Dega, built in memory of two of his queens, Rupamati and Rajamati.

Jagannath Temple

Built in 1563 by King Mahendra Malla atop a low plinth with four corner subsidiary shrines, this two-tiered temple features exquisitely carved erotic wooden roof struts.

Kaal Bhairav

A colossal 12-foot black stone relief sculpture of Kaal Bhairav, sculpted around the 6th century Licchavi era and installed in Durbar Square in the 17th century by King Pratap Malla.

Indrapur Temple

A rare open-plan upper balcony temple adjacent to the Narayan temple, historically used to display an image of Indra during Indra Jatra.

Narayan Temple

A three-tiered pagoda built on a four-level stepped brick base in the late 17th century, featuring a square cella and decorative upper roofs.

Kageshwor Mahadeva Temple

Erected around 1711 by Queen Bhuvanalakshmi, featuring an unusual fusion of a Newar lower temple with an upper stone Shikhara spire added after the 1934 earthquake.

Kotilingeshwor Mahadeva Temple

Built in 1562 by King Mahendra Malla, enshrining a four-faced chaturmukha linga of Shiva.

Maha Vishnu Temple

Built during the reign of King Jagajjaya Malla (1722-1736) as a memorial temple for his son Rajendra Malla.

Taleju Bhawani Temple

Built in 1564 by King Mahendra Malla on a twelve-stepped platform surrounded by 16 satellite shrines, this grand three-tiered gilded pagoda is the sacred protector temple of the Malla dynasty.

Makhan Pashupatinath Temple

Located at Makhan Tole, built by King Mahendra Malla for elderly devotees unable to travel to Pashupatinath, housing a five-faced Shiva lingam.

Hanuman Dhoka Palace and Museum

The royal palace complex containing historic courtyards (Nasal Chowk, Mul Chowk, Mohan Chowk) and museum galleries showcasing royal thrones, jewels, and coronation regalia.

name: Kathesimbhu Stupa
description:
Location:
Located in central Kathmandu at Shree Gha, approximately 650 meters north of Hanuman Dhoka Durbar Square, between Thamel and the historic core.

Existence:
The earliest inscription found here dates from 1551 CE, with major restorations undertaken during the reign of King Pratap Malla in the 17th century.

Description:
Also known as Shree Gha-Shanti Ghat Bajradhatu Mahachaitya, this stupa is an elegant miniature replica of Swayambhunath, complete with a whitewashed dome, painted harmika, and gilded spire. It houses a small Harati Mata shrine consecrated for worshippers unable to climb to Swayambhunath.

name: Seto Machchhindranath
description:
Location:
Located in the courtyard of Jana Bahal at Kel Tole, along the historic market street connecting Asan and Indra Chowk in central Kathmandu.

Existence:
Believed to have been established around the 10th century CE. Dedicated to Avalokiteshvara (Karunamaya), affectionately known locally as Janabaha Dyo.

Description:
A multi-tiered pagoda adorned with repousse bronze work and woodcarvings, revered jointly by Buddhists and Hindus. Inside sits the sacred white-faced deity. Each Chaitra, a 32-cubit-tall wooden chariot is pulled through Kathmandu in a vibrant three-day festival.

name: Indra Chowk
description:
Location:
Located at a major crossroads in central Kathmandu, intersecting the ancient India-Tibet trade route along Maru, Durbar Square, Makhan, Jana Bahal, Asan, and Naxal.

Existence:
Historically known as Wongha, Indra Chowk has served as a central ceremonial and marketplace square since the Licchavi and Malla dynasties.

Description:
A vibrant commercial square famous for cloth and spice merchants, centered around the temple of Akash Bhairav. The temple balcony displays the sacred mask of Bhairav during the Indra Jatra festival above bustling open-air street stalls.

name: Ranipokhari
description:
Location:
Located in central Kathmandu, bordered to the east by Ghantaghar (Clock Tower) and Tri-Chandra College, to the south by Ratna Park, and to the west by Durbar High School.

Existence:
Built in 1670 CE (1727 B.S.) by King Pratap Malla to console his queen after their son Chakravartendra Malla was fatally trampled by an elephant.

Description:
Spanning 180 meters by 140 meters across 62 ropanis, this historic pond features the central temple of Bal Gopaleshwor reached via a causeway, an elephant statue bearing King Pratap Malla and his sons, and four protective corner shrines.

name: Dharahara (Bhimsen Tower)
description:
Location:
Located at the center of Sundhara in downtown Kathmandu, adjacent to the historic royal sunken water spouts and close to New Road.

Existence:
First built in 1832 CE by Mukhtiyar Bhimsen Thapa under Queen Lalit Tripurasundari. Rebuilt after the 1934 and 2015 earthquakes, the newly reconstructed tower was opened in April 2021.

Description:
The reconstructed Dharahara rises 72 meters with 22 stories, featuring a traditional white minaret design, bronze finial, observation lifts, a 360-degree panoramic viewing gallery, museum, and landscaped memorial gardens.

name: Ratnapark
description:
Location:
Located in central Kathmandu, situated between Rani Pokhari to the north and the historic Tundikhel grounds to the south.

Existence:
Built during the 1960s under King Mahendra and named for Queen Ratna. Officially renamed Shankhadhar Udyan in 2020 in honor of national hero Shankhadhar Sakhwa.

Description:
A central green public park featuring shaded walkways, manicured flowerbeds, fountains, and statues of Shankhadhar Sakhwa and Queen Ratna, acting as a tranquil pedestrian refuge amidst the city's main transit corridors.

name: Thamel
description:
Location:
Located in north-central Kathmandu, situated immediately north of the old palace quarter and Kaiser Mahal.

Existence:
Originating from the ancient Newar monastic locality 'Tha Bahi', Thamel evolved from a quiet historical enclave into Nepal's foremost tourist hub since the late 1960s.

Description:
A world-renowned neighborhood featuring narrow alleys filled with trekking gear shops, handicraft emporiums, bakeries, cafes, boutique hotels, and lively acoustic music bars, interspersed with peaceful traditional courtyards (bahals).

name: Garden of Dreams
description:
Location:
Located inside the Kaiser Mahal compound on Tridevi Sadak in central Kathmandu, directly opposite the gates of Narayanhity Palace.

Existence:
Created in 1920 CE by Field Marshal Kaiser Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana and restored between 2000 and 2007 with support from the Austrian Government.

Description:
A 6,895-square-meter neoclassical Edwardian garden of the six seasons (Swapna Bagaicha), featuring marble balustrades, classical pavilions, sunken lily ponds, an amphitheater, and the adjoining historic Kaiser Library.

name: Narayanhity Palace Museum
description:
Location:
Located at the northern terminus of Durbar Marg in central Kathmandu, adjacent to Keshar Mahal.

Existence:
Historic seat of royal residences; the modern palace was built by King Mahendra in 1963, designed by American architect Benjamin Polk. In 2008, it opened to the public as a national museum.

Description:
Covering 3,794 square meters of floor space within expansive grounds, the museum features 52 state rooms, the ceremonial Throne Room, coronation jewels, state banquet halls, and historic royal artifacts.

name: National Museum (Chhauni)
description:
Location:
Located at Chhauni along the eastern bank of the Vishnumati River near the western foot of Swayambhunath hill.

Existence:
Established in 1824 CE by Prime Minister Bhimsen Thapa as an arsenal house (Silkhana), converted into the Nepal Museum in 1939, and renamed the National Museum in 1968.

Description:
Spanning 50 ropanis of gardens, the museum comprises the Historical Art Gallery (exhibiting Licchavi and Malla stone and wood sculptures), the Buddhist Art Gallery, and the Natural History and Military Wing with historic weaponry and rare coins.

name: Pashupatinath Temple
description:
Location:
Located on the sacred banks of the Bagmati River in eastern Kathmandu, approximately 5 km northeast of the city center.

Existence:
Enlisted as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. Historical records trace the shrine to 400 CE, with major reconstructions by King Supuspa Deva, King Shivadeva (1099-1126 CE), and King Bhupalendra Malla.

Description:
The holiest Hindu shrine in Nepal, dedicated to Lord Shiva as Pashupati. Spanning 246 hectares with 518 temples and shrines, the main pagoda features a two-tiered gilded copper roof, four silver-sheeted doors, and a five-faced stone Mukhalinga, alongside the Arya Ghat and Mrigasthali deer forest.

name: Swoyambhunath
description:
Location:
Perched atop a conical hilltop in western Kathmandu, commanding panoramic views across the valley.

Existence:
Enlisted as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. Founded in the early 5th century CE by King Vrsadeva, with mythological roots in the Swayambhu Purana describing the primordial lotus flame.

Description:
A revered sacred stupa complex featuring a whitewashed dome, harmika with the all-seeing eyes of Buddha, and 13 gilded tiers. The hilltop is home to Harati Mata temple, chaityas, Tibetan monasteries, and the famous resident monkeys.

name: Bouddhanath
description:
Location:
Located approximately 11 km northeast of central Kathmandu along the historic trans-Himalayan trade route to Tibet.

Existence:
Enlisted as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. Founded around the 6th century CE by Licchavi King Shivadeva or King Manadeva, known in Nepal Bhasa as 'Khasti'.

Description:
One of the largest spherical stupas in the world, featuring a massive dome with a 100-foot diameter rising 141 feet over a stepped mandala platform. Circled by 147 prayer wheel niches and over 50 Tibetan Buddhist monasteries.

name: Budhanilkantha Temple
description:
Location:
Located at the northern edge of the Kathmandu Valley at the foot of the Shivapuri Hill in Budhanilkantha, about 10 km north of the city center.

Existence:
Dates back to the 7th-century Licchavi period during the reign of King Vishnugupta or King Pratapaditya.

Description:
Famous for its monumental 5-meter-long stone statue of Lord Vishnu reclining upon the coiled serpent Shesha in the middle of a recessed pool. Carved from a single basalt monolith, it is the focal point of Haribodhini Ekadashi.

name: Balaju (Baisdhara) Park
description:
Location:
Located approximately 5 km northwest of Kathmandu at the base of the forested Nagarjun hill.

Existence:
Built in the mid-18th century by King Jaya Prakash Malla with 21 water spouts; King Rana Bahadur Shah added the 22nd spout and installed a reclining Vishnu idol in 1774.

Description:
A serene public garden featuring 22 stone crocodile-headed water spouts flowing with natural mountain spring water, swimming pools, shaded lawns, and shrines, drawing festive crowds during Chaitra Purnima.

name: Tribhuwan Park
description:
Location:
Located in Thankot at the southwestern entrance gateway of the Kathmandu Valley along the Tribhuwan Highway.

Existence:
Established in 1972 CE by King Birendra in honor of his grandfather, King Tribhuwan, who led the democratic transformation of Nepal in 1951.

Description:
Covering 1.3 square kilometers of rolling hills, the park features pine groves, picnic pavilions, walking paths, and a central bronze statue of King Tribhuwan.

name: Jal Binayak (Koina Ganesh), Chobhar
description:
Location:
Located on the western bank of the Bagmati River at the historic Chobhar gorge in southwest Kathmandu.

Existence:
One of the four cardinal Binayak temples of the Kathmandu Valley. The pagoda was built in 1602 CE and renovated by King Bhupalendra Malla in 1689.

Description:
A three-tiered pagoda built over a natural, uncarved stone rock formation worshipped as Lord Ganesh, set against the dramatic limestone cliffs of the Chobhar gorge.

name: Taudaha
description:
Location:
Located approximately 6 km southwest of Lagankhel along the road to Pharping in southern Kathmandu.

Existence:
According to mythology, when Manjushri cut the Chobhar gorge to drain the valley's ancient lake, King Karkotak, king of serpents (Nagas), was granted Taudaha as his permanent underwater kingdom.

Description:
A pristine 4-hectare natural freshwater lake fringed with willows and reeds, serving as an important ecological wetland sanctuary for migratory Himalayan birds and a sacred site during Nag Panchami.

name: Shesh Narayan, Pharping
description:
Location:
Located near the ancient town of Pharping, approximately 20 km southwest of central Kathmandu.

Existence:
One of the four guardian Narayan temples of the valley, dating back to the Licchavi era with major structures rebuilt in the 17th century.

Description:
Nestled beneath towering limestone cliffs, this holy temple features spring-fed ponds filled with fish, fine Licchavi stone statues of Sheshashayi Vishnu, and meditation caves linked to Guru Padmasambhava.

name: Pharping Hydropower Station, Soukhel Pharping
description:
Location:
Located in Pharping, approximately 13 km south of central Kathmandu.

Existence:
Constructed starting in 1907 CE and inaugurated on May 22, 1911 by King Prithvi Bir Bikram Shah Dev. It is Nepal's first hydropower station and the second oldest in Asia.

Description:
Originally producing 500 kW of electricity using water from spring sources, the plant electrified the royal palace and Kathmandu. Today it is preserved as an open living museum of early 20th-century industrial engineering.

Pharping Reservoir & Intake

The masonry header reservoir and hydraulic water channels situated on the hill above the station, which supplied water under pressure down the historic steel penstocks.

name: Dakshinkali Temple
description:
Location:
Located in a forested rocky cleft 22 km south of Kathmandu, approximately 1 km beyond the village of Pharping.

Existence:
Established in the 14th century and renovated in the 17th century by King Pratap Malla following a divine dream.

Description:
One of Nepal's most prominent Shakti Peethas, dedicated to Goddess Kali. Set at the confluence of two sacred streams, the open-air temple attracts thousands of worshippers, particularly during Tuesdays, Saturdays, and the Dashain festival.

name: Sundarijal
description:
Location:
Located 15 km northeast of Kathmandu at the southern boundary of Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park.

Existence:
Named from 'Sundari' (beautiful) and 'Jal' (water), historically developed in the 1930s as a primary water supply and hydroelectric reservoir for the capital.

Description:
A scenic mountain getaway celebrated for its roaring waterfalls, boulder-strewn streams, and oak-pine forests. It serves as the main trekking trailhead for Helambu and Langtang.

name: Bagh bhairav, Kirtipur
description:
Location:
Located on the crest of the historic hill-town of Kirtipur, 7 km southwest of central Kathmandu at an elevation of 1,405 meters.

Existence:
Founded in the 16th century by King Sadashiva Deva (1574-1581 CE), dedicated to Lord Bhairav in the form of a tiger (Bagh).

Description:
A prominent three-tiered pagoda standing in a wide brick courtyard. Beneath the second-tier eaves hang real swords and muskets captured from the soldiers of King Prithvi Narayan Shah during the 18th-century battles of Kirtipur.

name: Adinath Lokeshwor , Chobhar
description:
Location:
Located on the ridge of Chobhar village, approximately 6 km southwest of Kathmandu, overlooking the Bagmati river valley.

Existence:
Founded in the 15th century and rebuilt in 1640 CE, associated with the 8th-century Buddhist nun Gelongma Palmo.

Description:
A three-tiered pagoda dedicated to Red Avalokiteshvara, revered by both Buddhists and Hindus. The temple's exterior walls are covered in hundreds of metal plates, pots, and utensils nailed by newlyweds for marital bliss.

name: Patan Durbar Square
description:
Location:
Located at Mangal Bazaar in the historic center of Patan (Lalitpur), bordered by Pulchowk to the west and Sundhara to the east.

Existence:
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. Founded during the Licchavi period, it achieved architectural grandeur under the Malla kings of Patan during the 16th to 18th centuries.

Description:
Renowned for its red-brick courtyards, stone temples, and bronze metalcraft, the square encompasses three major royal chowks and masterwork pagoda and shikhara shrines.

Krishna Mandir

Constructed in 1637 by King Siddhi Narasimha Malla, this three-tiered stone Shikhara temple is an architectural marvel. It features 21 stone pinnacles and detailed narrative friezes depicting the Mahabharata and Ramayana.

Mul Chowk

The oldest and most sacred of Patan's royal courtyards, Mul Chowk is dedicated to Goddess Taleju Bhawani. It is framed by two-storey wings with intricate gilded repousse toranas and strut carvings.

Sundari Chowk

Built in 1647, Sundari Chowk is renowned for the sunken royal bath Tusha Hiti, lined with 72 exquisite stone carvings of tantric deities, guarded by stone sculptures of Hanuman, Ganesh, and Narsimha.

Keshav Chowk

Located in the northern palace wing, Keshav Narayan Chowk now houses the renowned Patan Museum. The courtyard features a central gilded temple of Vishnu and intricate golden window facades.

Bhandarkhal

The royal palace garden and tank situated behind Sundari Chowk, historically serving as a water storage and pleasure retreat for the Malla kings.

Patan Museum

Housed within the restored 17th-century palace, the museum exhibits one of Asia's finest collections of bronze and copper sacred art, showcasing Hindu and Buddhist iconographic traditions.

Bhimsen Temple

Built in 1680 by King Srinivasa Malla, this three-tiered pagoda temple honors Bhimsen, the god of trade and commerce, featuring an upper-floor worship sanctum.

Vishwanath Temple

Built in 1627 by King Siddhi Narasimha Malla, this two-tiered Shiva temple is guarded by two monumental stone elephants at its entrance stairs.

Hari Shankar Temple

Constructed in 1704, this three-tiered pagoda honors the syncretic deity Hari Shankar, representing half Vishnu and half Shiva.

Taleju Temple

A soaring multi-roofed palace tower dedicated to Taleju Bhawani, the lineage deity of the Malla kings.

Char Narayan (Jagannarayan) Temple

Built in 1565, this two-tiered brick pagoda is the oldest temple in Patan Durbar Square, enshrining four stone manifestations of Vishnu.

name: Rato Machhindranath, Tabahal Patan
description:
Location:
Located at Tabahal (Machhindra Bahal), approximately 400 meters south of Patan Durbar Square in Lalitpur.

Existence:
The present three-tiered temple dates from 1673 CE, built over an ancient 6th-century foundation dedicated to Karunamaya / Bungadyo.

Description:
Standing in an expansive brick courtyard, the temple features rich woodcarvings, metal repousse doorways, and prayer wheels. It is the central staging ground for the month-long Boto Jatra chariot festival.

name: Hiranya Varna Mahabihar (Golden Temple), Kwabahal Patan
description:
Location:
Located at Kwa Bahal, approximately 400 meters northwest of Patan Durbar Square.

Existence:
Founded in the 12th century by King Bhaskaradeva, with documented inscriptions dating from 1409 CE.

Description:
A three-tiered gilded monastery featuring gilded copper roofs, silver repousse shrines, and statues of lions, elephants, and Garuda. The inner sanctum enshrines Shakyamuni Buddha.

name: Kumbheshwara Temple
description:
Location:
Located at Konti (Kumbheshwor), approximately 500 meters north of Patan Durbar Square.

Existence:
Built in 1392 CE by King Jayasthiti Malla, it is the only five-tiered pagoda temple in Patan and one of just three in the entire Kathmandu Valley.

Description:
Dedicated to Lord Shiva as Kumbheshwara ('Lord of the Water Pot'), this soaring five-tiered pagoda features spring-fed ponds believed to connect directly to the sacred alpine lake of Gosaikunda.

Bagalamukhi Temple

A sacred yellow-painted shrine on the southern edge of the Kumbheshwara courtyard dedicated to Goddess Bagalamukhi, visited especially on Thursdays for spiritual protection and fulfillment of wishes.

name: Mahabouddha, Patan
description:
Location:
Located in the narrow traditional streets of Sundhara, approximately 500 meters southeast of Patan Durbar Square.

Existence:
Construction was initiated in 1585 CE by priest Abhaya Raj Shakya after visiting Bodh Gaya, and completed in 1601 CE.

Description:
Known as the 'Temple of the Thousand Buddhas', every terracotta brick of this tall shikhara spire is stamped with an individual image of the Buddha, set in a cozy residential bahal.

name: Rudra Varna Mahabihar (Ukubahal)
description:
Location:
Located at Ukubahal in southeast Patan, adjacent to Mahabouddha, about 600 meters from Patan Durbar Square.

Existence:
Founded by Licchavi King Shivadeva (590-604 CE) as one of Patan's five major monasteries and renovated in the 12th century by King Rudradeva.

Description:
One of Patan's oldest monasteries, the two-tiered courtyard is rich in bronze statuary, stone lions, peacocks, elephants, and historic ritual masterpieces.

name: Central Zoo, Jawalakhel
description:
Location:
Located at Jawalakhel in Lalitpur, approximately 1.8 km southwest of Patan Durbar Square.

Existence:
Established in 1932 CE as a private menagerie by Rana Prime Minister Juddha Shumsher, opened to the public in 1956, and managed by the National Trust for Nature Conservation since 1995.

Description:
Nepal's only national zoological garden, covering 6 hectares centered around a historic royal pond, home to over 800 animals including Royal Bengal tigers, rhinos, red pandas, and Asian elephants.

name: Ashokan Stupas, Patan
description:
Location:
Situated at the four cardinal perimeter points of Patan: Pulchowk (West), Lagankhel (South), Imadol (East), and Sankhamul (North).

Existence:
Attributed by tradition to Emperor Ashoka of India during his pilgrimage to the valley in 250 BCE; historically dating to the 4th-5th century CE.

Description:
Four circular earthen and brick hemispherical stupas marking the sacred boundaries of historic Patan, each housing Dhyani Buddha niches facing the cardinal directions.

Southern Stupa (Lagan Thur)

The largest of the four Ashokan stupas, situated at Lagankhel, capped with a modern harmika and surrounded by stone chaityas.

Western Stupa (Pucho Thur)

Located atop the hillock of Pulchowk, featuring four Buddha niches facing the cardinal directions.

Eastern Stupa (Teta Thur)

Located along the road to Imadol, preserving a massive earthen mound covered in brick and grass.

Northern Stupa (Ibahi Thur)

Located near Sankhamul on the northern boundary of Patan, crowned with painted eyes and a gilded finial.

name: Godawari
description:
Location:
Located at the foot of Mount Phulchowki (2,715m) in Godawari (1,515m), about 10 km southeast of Patan.

Existence:
The National Botanical Garden was inaugurated in October 1962 by King Mahendra, designed with British botanical experts.

Description:
Covering 82 hectares of lush forested land with more than 500 species of native plants, orchid houses, fern gardens, natural streams, and the sacred Godawari Kunda spring.

name: Bajrabarahi, Chapagaon
description:
Location:
Located approximately 8 km south of Patan at the junction of Thecho, Chapagaon, and Jharuwarasi.

Existence:
Established in the 15th century by King Bhuvanamalla in 1664 CE within an ancient sacred woodland.

Description:
One of the four cardinal Barahi temples of the valley, dedicated to the boar-headed goddess Bajrabarahi. Set within an 18-hectare natural forest, the two-tiered pagoda features no pinnacle (gajur), an intentional architectural oddity symbolising humility, surrounded by stone idols and prayer bells.

name: Nagdaha, Dhapakhel
description:
Location:
Located in Dhapakhel village, approximately 5 km south of Lagankhel in Lalitpur.

Existence:
Associated in valley folklore with serpent king Karkotak and natural springs from Gaukhureshwor Mahadev.

Description:
A 5-hectare freshwater lake ringed with green banks and water lilies, serving as a bird-watching habitat and an auspicious pilgrimage site during Nag Panchami.

name: Santaneshwor Mahadev, Jharuwarashi Badegaon
description:
Location:
Perched on a conical hilltop in Jharuwarashi, Godawari Municipality, about 10 km south of Patan at 1,400 meters elevation.

Existence:
An ancient Shakti Peetha site associated in the Swasthani Vrata Katha with the falling of Sati Devi's breast bone.

Description:
Dedicated to Lord Shiva, revered especially by childless couples praying for children. A forest stairway leads up to the summit shrine, which commands 360-degree views across the southern valley.

name: Karya Vinayak
description:
Location:
Located on a hillock in Bungamati, Lalitpur, approximately 10 km south of Kathmandu.

Existence:
Dedicated in Nepal Sambat 781 (1661 CE) under King Srinivasa Malla and the local guthi.

Description:
One of the four cardinal Vinayaka shrines of the valley. Worshippers pray here before starting new tasks or travels to eliminate obstacles, overlooking rural fields and the Bagmati river.

name: Sikali, Khokana
description:
Location:
Located in an open plateau outside the mustard-oil-pressing village of Khokana, about 10 km south of Kathmandu.

Existence:
An ancient animist and tantric Newar sanctuary dating from the early medieval period, sacred to the goddess Rudrayani (Sikali Devi).

Description:
An open shrine set amidst terraced fields with views toward Chandragiri. Famous for the Sikali Jatra, an ancient festival celebrated with masked dances in place of conventional Dashain rituals.

name: Rato Machhindranath, Bungamati
description:
Location:
Located at the historic central square of Bungamati village, overlooking the Bagmati River in southern Lalitpur.

Existence:
The ancestral home of Karunamaya / Bungadyo (Rato Machhindranath), dating back to the 7th century under King Narendra Deva.

Description:
A soaring shikhara and pagoda temple set in a large brick courtyard where the deity of rain and harvest resides for six months of each year following the Patan chariot festival.

name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square
description:
Location:
Located in the center of Bhaktapur city, approximately 13 km east of central Kathmandu.

Existence:
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. Seat of the Malla kingdom of Bhaktapur from the 12th century until 1769.

Description:
A medieval royal palace plaza renowned for its brick architecture, woodcarvings, and metalwork, encompassing Durbar Square, Taumadhi Square, Dattatreya Square, and Pottery Square.

55 Window Palace (Pachpanna Jhyale Durbar)

Built in 1427 by King Yaksha Malla and remodeled by King Bhupatindra Malla in the 17th century, this royal palace is famed for its continuous row of 55 intricately carved sandalwood windows.

Golden Gate (Lu Dhowka)

Crafted in 1753 by King Ranjit Malla, this gilded repousse gateway is acclaimed by art historians as one of the finest masterpieces of metal art in the entire world, leading into the Taleju royal courtyard.

National Art Museum

Housed in the western palace wing, the museum preserves rare palm-leaf manuscripts, ancient stone sculptures, and Buddhist thangkas.

Vatsala Durga Temple

A 17th-century Shikhara-style stone temple dedicated to Goddess Vatsala, featuring the famous 'Taleju Bell of the Barking Dogs'.

Pashupatinath (Yaksheshwor) Temple

Built by King Yaksha Malla in 1475 as a replica of Pashupatinath, featuring celebrated erotic wooden roof struts.

Chyasalin Mandap

An octagonal two-storey pavilion reconstructed after the 1934 earthquake, historically used as a royal viewing pavilion and poetry retreat.

name: Nyatapola Temple
description:
Location:
Located at the northern end of Taumadhi Square in central Bhaktapur.

Existence:
Commissioned by King Bhupatindra Malla in 1701-1702 CE, constructed in an astonishing seven months.

Description:
Rising over 30 meters on a five-tier plinth, Nyatapola ('Five-Storied Roof') is Nepal's tallest pagoda temple, dedicated to Siddhi Lakshmi and guarded by stone pairs of wrestlers, elephants, lions, griffins, and goddesses.

name: Bhairavnath Temple
description:
Location:
Located on the eastern side of Taumadhi Square, adjacent to the Nyatapola temple.

Existence:
Built as a one-storey pagoda by King Jagat Jyoti Malla and enlarged to three storeys in 1717 CE by King Bhupatindra Malla.

Description:
A broad three-tiered rectangular pagoda dedicated to Kashi Bhairav (Naso Dyo), decorated with copper roofs and struts, serving as the center for the Bisket Jatra chariot tug-of-war.

name: Dattatreya Temple
description:
Location:
Located at the eastern end of Tachapal Tole (Dattatreya Square) in Bhaktapur.

Existence:
Built in 1427 CE by King Yaksha Malla and remodeled in 1458 CE by King Raya Malla.

Description:
A stout three-tiered pagoda honoring Dattatreya (the composite Trimurti of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva), traditionally believed to have been carved from a single tree trunk.

name: Siddha Pokhari
description:
Location:
Located near the western entrance gate of Bhaktapur, just outside the historic urban core.

Existence:
Built in the 15th century during the reign of King Yaksha Malla over older medieval water foundations.

Description:
The oldest and largest rectangular artificial pond in Bhaktapur (275m by 92m), known locally as Ta Pukhu, surrounded by shade trees and stone god niches.

name: Rani Pokhari
description:
Location:
Located immediately west of Siddha Pokhari near the old western entrance to Bhaktapur.

Existence:
Commissioned by King Jagat Jyoti Malla in the early 17th century, approximately 40 years before Kathmandu's Rani Pokhari.

Description:
A restored historic brick-lined water reservoir decorated with stone steps and water spouts, forming part of Bhaktapur's traditional community water harvesting system.

name: Changu Narayan, Bhaktapur
description:
Location:
Perched on a forested ridge at Dolagiri (Changu), about 12 km east of Kathmandu and 6 km north of Bhaktapur.

Existence:
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. Houses Nepal's oldest stone inscription, erected in 464 CE by Licchavi King Manadeva.

Description:
The oldest Hindu temple complex in the valley, featuring a two-tiered pagoda dedicated to Lord Vishnu, celebrated for masterwork Licchavi stone statues including Vishwaroop and Vishnu Vikrant.

name: Surya Vinayak, Bhaktapur
description:
Location:
Located in a pine-covered hill in Sipadol, approximately 2 km south of Bhaktapur city.

Existence:
Established over 1,500 years ago during the Licchavi period and renovated under the Malla dynasty.

Description:
One of the four cardinal Vinayak temples of the valley, dedicated to the 'Rising Sun Ganesh' oriented to receive the day's first sun rays, visited by parents praying for speech development in young children.

name: Doleshwor Mahadev, Sipadol Bhaktapur
description:
Location:
Located in Sipadol, Bhaktapur district, approximately 20 km east of Kathmandu.

Existence:
Recognized in 2009 by the head priest of Kedarnath as the long-lost head of the holy bull incarnation of Lord Shiva from Kedarnath, India.

Description:
A tranquil pilgrimage shrine nestled between lush wooded hills, linking Mahabharata pilgrimage traditions between Kedarnath in Uttarakhand and the Kathmandu Valley.

name: Kailashnath Mahadev Statue, Sanga
description:
Location:
Located on the border between Bhaktapur and Kavrepalanchok districts at Sanga, about 20 km east of Kathmandu.

Existence:
Constructed between 2003 and 2010 by modern engineers and sculptors.

Description:
Rising 143 feet (43.5 meters), this is the second tallest statue of Lord Shiva in the world, sculpted of copper, zinc, and concrete, depicting Shiva holding his trident over the valley rim.

name: Nagarkot
description:
Location:
Located along the eastern rim of the Kathmandu Valley at an elevation of 2,195 meters, 32 km northeast of Kathmandu and 20 km east of Bhaktapur.

Existence:
Historically an ancient hilltop garrison monitoring eastern trade routes, evolved in the 20th century into Nepal's foremost panoramic mountain hill station.

Description:
World-renowned for spectacular sunrise and sunset panoramas stretching from Dhaulagiri in the west past Everest to Kanchenjunga, surrounded by pine forests and terraced hillsides.
